claude_proposed_widenings.name: MagicItemRecord
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: UnitRecord has no magic_item kind. The tracer's exhaustive switch on unit.kind throws on any value other than spell, class_feature, mastery. A MagicItemRecord needs at minimum: id, name, provenance, description, kind: 'magic_item', attunement requirement, and a mechanics payload.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: Wondrous Item, Uncommon — item is neither a spell, class feature, nor mastery.

claude_proposed_widenings.name: magic_item_activation family
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: Magic items have a distinct activation pattern: the item itself is a persistent resource container (charges or consumable cards); activation draws from that resource and fires an effect. This does not reduce to SpellMechanics (no level/school/castingTime/components/duration header), ClassFeatureMechanics (no class/acquiredAtLevel), or MasteryMechanics (no weapon-hit trigger).
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: You can take a Magic action to draw a card at random from the deck and throw it to the ground... An illusion... forms over the thrown card and remains until dispelled.

claude_proposed_widenings.name: create_illusion
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: The Deck creates an illusory creature — not a real companion, not an inert object. SRD specifies it looks and behaves like a real creature but can do no harm, objects pass through it, and it is identifiable by a DC 15 INT (Investigation) check. These properties make it mechanically distinct from create_object or create_companion. A create_illusion atom would need to carry harmless and passable flags and link to the ability_check identification gate.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: The illusory creature created by the card looks and behaves like a real creature of its kind, except that it can do no harm. [...] objects pass through it.

claude_proposed_widenings.name: random_table_resolution
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: The creature created is determined by rolling on a d100 table at draw time. No existing surface type models non-deterministic table-resolved outcomes. This is not a save_gate or attack_roll — it is a DM-visible random selection from a closed enumerated table.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: An illusion of a creature, determined by rolling on the Deck of Illusions table, forms over the thrown card.

claude_proposed_widenings.name: per_card_use_count
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: Each card in the deck is individually consumable: once its illusion ends, its image disappears and the card cannot be used again. The existing UseCountResource models a refillable pool; deck-card depletion is a non-refilling, per-instance resource where the total cap is itself randomised at acquisition ('usually missing 1d20-1 cards'). The charge atom is closest but charge resources are assumed uniform and refillable.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: When the illusion ends, the image on its card disappears, and that card can't be used again. [...] A deck found as treasure is usually missing 1d20 − 1 cards.
